scope: Greater Houston suburbs (Fort Bend, Montgomery, Brazoria, Galveston counties) - basic needs

records.name: Utility Assistance
records.description_en: Fort Bend County Social Services can help pay a utility bill when you have a shut-off notice or a bill you must pay. Case workers also help connect you to other benefits.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For Fort Bend County residents who meet program guidelines. Adults 18+ who are not working and not in school must show they are registered with Workforce Solutions/TWC or have a doctor's proof of disability.
documents_needed: Social Security card, driver license, or ID for head of household and spouse (metal Social Security cards not accepted)
Proof of income for the past 30 days for everyone in the household
Proof of Workforce Solutions/TWC registration or doctor's proof of disability for unemployed adults 18+ not in school
Termination (shut-off) notice or bill requiring payment
Receipts for all bills paid in the last 30 days
records.how_to_apply: Call the Rosenberg office (281) 238-3502 or the Missouri City office (281) 403-8050 to set up an appointment. Appointments are required.
records.notes: Second office: 307 Texas Parkway, Suite 235, Missouri City, TX 77459, (281) 403-8050, Mon-Fri 8am-5pm (from the Social Services Contact Us page). The county does not pay utility deposits, rental deposits, or bills transferred from another address. Email: SocialServicesInbox@fortbendcountytx.gov. Social Services also offers case management, Benefits Bank, indigent burials, and veterans help (Operation Fort Bend Heroes).

records.name: Comprehensive Energy Assistance Program (CEAP) - Fort Bend County
records.description_en: Helps low-income households pay electric, gas, or propane bills. There is also crisis help when your power is off or about to be shut off.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income households in Fort Bend County (the agency also serves other nearby counties). Priority is given to people over 60, people with disabilities, and homes with children under 5.
records.how_to_apply: Use the 'Get Help / Aplicar Aqui' application on ccaction.com, or call the Stafford office. Check the website for whether Fort Bend applications are open.
records.notes: Combined Community Action is the CEAP provider for Fort Bend County (confirmed by GCCAC transition notice). A search summary of the ccaction.com CEAP page said Fort Bend applications were limited due to high volume and open only to high-priority applicants (60+, disabled, children under 5); a 979-540-2988 number was listed for Fort Bend application requests. Confirm current status by phone.

records.name: Utility Assistance Program (CEAP)
records.description_en: Helps pay electric, gas, or propane bills for low-income households. It does not pay water bills.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For households in Harris, Brazoria, or Galveston County with income at or below the program limit (for 2026: $23,940 for 1 person, $32,460 for 2, $40,980 for 3, $49,500 for 4). One application per household per calendar year.

eligibility_rules.residency_required: Brazoria, Galveston, or Harris County resident

documents_needed: Social Security card for all household members
Proof of income from the last 30 days for all household members 18+
Photo ID (driver license, passport, or school ID)
Proof of citizenship or legal residency (birth certificate, passport, or naturalization certificate)
Current electric, gas, or propane bill
records.how_to_apply: Apply online through the BakerRipley portal when applications are open, or call the Utility Assistance Hotline for an in-person appointment.
records.notes: Page said applications were closed and expected to reopen Monday, November 9, with in-person appointments starting October 27; the portal takes about 4,000 applications per opening. Decisions in about 6 weeks. Funding is limited; high energy users get priority. Funded by TDHCA.

records.name: Utility Assistance Bill Pay Program (CEAP)
records.description_en: Helps eligible households pay electric, natural gas, or propane bills.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income households in Montgomery County and other Brazos Valley counties who meet state and federal program rules. You must reapply each year.
documents_needed: Signed application
Proof of citizenship
Photo ID for household members over 18
Proof of income for adults (or Income Declaration form)
Copy of utility bill(s)
Utility provider release form if required
records.how_to_apply: Apply through the BVCAP online application portal or by appointment. Applications are taken by appointment only.
records.notes: Main office is in Bryan; no separate Montgomery County office was listed. Alternate phone (979) 595-2850; Montgomery fax (936) 856-7069; email bvcapcontact@bvcog.org. Documents must be resubmitted each year.

records.name: Rental and Utility Assistance
records.organization: Greater Coastal Community Action Council (Galveston County Community Action Council)
records.description_en: Case managers help pay electric, gas, water bills, and rent for families in financial hardship when funds are available.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For residents of Brazoria, Fort Bend, Galveston, or Wharton County facing financial hardship. Proof of income is required.

eligibility_rules.residency_required: Brazoria, Fort Bend, Galveston, or Wharton County resident

documents_needed: Proof of income
records.how_to_apply: Call or email the case managers to ask about help and current funding.
records.notes: Help depends on available funding. Email clientsupport@gccac.org. GCCAC is no longer the CEAP provider (since 2021): Galveston/Brazoria CEAP goes through BakerRipley, Fort Bend CEAP through Combined Community Action.

records.name: Montgomery County Food Bank
records.description_en: The food bank supplies more than 90 partner pantries, drive-thru mobile markets, senior deliveries, and school pantries across Montgomery County. Use their Find Food Map to find food near you.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For Montgomery County residents facing hunger. Each partner pantry may have its own rules.
records.how_to_apply: Use the Find Food Map on mcfoodbank.org to find a partner pantry or mobile market, or call the food bank. Food is not handed out at the warehouse.
records.notes: Mobile markets are drive-thru, first-come first-served, serving 150-250 families each. Someone else may be able to pick up food for a family that cannot drive (depends on the partner agency). Email info@mcfoodbank.org.

records.name: Galveston County Food Bank On-Site Pantry and Mobile Distributions
records.description_en: Free groceries at the on-site pantry in Texas City and at mobile food truck stops around the county. They also offer food packs for kids in summer and help for homebound people.
records.eligibility_summary_en: The on-site pantry is for households that meet TEFAP income guidelines. No ID or documents are needed at mobile distributions.
records.how_to_apply: Visit the on-site pantry during open hours, or check the mobile calendar on the website for drive-thru distribution sites. Call ahead to confirm hours.
records.notes: Programs include Kidz Pacz (summer food packs for kids), Homebound Nutritional Outreach, mobile food trucks, and SNAP/social services referrals. Admin office: 213 6th Street N, Texas City (Mon-Fri 8am-4pm). Updates posted on Facebook/Instagram.

records.name: Dream Pantry and Crisis Resources
records.description_en: A food pantry in Clute that also delivers food to seniors, sends food home with kids (KidFuel), and offers crisis resources and a technology center.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For Brazoria County families who need food and support.
records.how_to_apply: Visit or call the Dream Center during office hours to ask about the pantry and other programs.
records.notes: Email info@bcdreamcenter.org. Some directories list the address as 792 Brazosport Blvd S; the official site says 794. Pantry-specific hours may differ from office hours; call ahead.

records.name: Brazosport Cares Food Pantry
records.description_en: Free food pantry with locations in Freeport and Sweeny for people in the Brazosport area of Brazoria County.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For residents of the Brazosport area of Brazoria County.
records.how_to_apply: Go to the Freeport or Sweeny pantry during distribution hours, or call the main office with questions.
records.hours: Freeport pantry: Tuesdays & Thursdays 9am-11:30am; 2nd & 4th Thursday 4pm-6pm. Office: Monday-Thursday 9am-4pm
records.notes: Main office: 916 North Gulf Blvd, Freeport, TX 77541. Sweeny pantry: 111 W. Third St., Sweeny, TX 77480, (979) 205-1021, Tuesdays 9:30am-12pm & 2pm-5pm, Wednesdays 9:30am-12pm. Eligibility details and required documents were not listed; call ahead.

records.name: Meals on Wheels and Senior Centers
records.organization: Fort Bend Seniors Meals on Wheels
records.description_en: Delivers free meals to homebound seniors (a hot meal Monday-Wednesday plus frozen meals for the weekend) and serves lunch at 6 senior centers. Rides to the centers are available as needed.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people age 60 or older in Fort Bend or Waller County. There is no income limit. Home delivery is for seniors who are homebound and cannot safely cook.

eligibility_rules.residency_required: Fort Bend or Waller County resident

records.how_to_apply: Call to request meal delivery for yourself or a loved one, or fill out the client referral form online.
records.notes: Senior Center Coordinator: (281) 633-7058. Also offers friendly calls/visits and pet assistance.

records.name: Katy Food Center (Food Pantry)
records.description_en: Free groceries through a car food line for registered clients in the Katy area, including parts of Fort Bend County.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people who live in KCM's service ZIP codes (77084 KISD only, 77094, 77406, 77407, 77423, 77441, 77449, 77450, 77464, 77476, 77485, 77493, 77494) and complete a Social Services assessment.

eligibility_rules.residency_required: Resident of a Katy-area ZIP code served by KCM

documents_needed: Completed application
Copies of documents listed on the KCM application
records.how_to_apply: Pick up or download an application from Social Services, return it with copies of your documents, then schedule an appointment. After you register, use the car food line.
records.hours: Car food line: Monday-Thursday 8:30am-12pm (registered clients only)
records.notes: Also serves Harris and Waller County ZIPs. Clients outside the service area have limited visits.

records.name: Social Services Financial Assistance (Rent, Mortgage, Utilities)
records.description_en: Case managers can help with rent, mortgage, and utility bills when grant money is available, and help people apply for SNAP, Medicaid, CHIP, and other benefits.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people living in KCM's Katy-area service ZIP codes (77084 KISD only, 77094, 77406, 77407, 77423, 77441, 77449, 77450, 77464, 77476, 77493, 77494) who pass a Social Services assessment.

eligibility_rules.residency_required: Resident of a Katy-area ZIP code served by KCM

documents_needed: Completed Financial Assistance application
Copies of documents listed on the application
records.how_to_apply: Download the application, bring it back in person with copies of your documents, then schedule an appointment. No walk-in financial assistance.
records.notes: Financial help only when grant funds are available. Also offers free mental health counseling (ext. 209 at 281-391-5261) and veterans help (Help-A-Hero, 281-712-8314). KCM 24/7 domestic violence hotline: (281) 391-4357.

records.name: Food Pantry and Family Services
records.description_en: Offers a food pantry, weekend food backpacks for kids, grocery delivery for homebound seniors, mobile pantry market days, and family services such as help with basic needs.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For individuals and families facing food insecurity or a sudden hardship in their service area.
records.how_to_apply: Call Interfaith of The Woodlands or visit the 'Get Assistance' section of their website to ask about services.
records.notes: Programs include Nutrition Every Weekend (kids' backpacks), Seniors Eating Well (grocery delivery), On The Go Market Days (mobile pantry), and Veggie Village. Service-area ZIP codes and required documents were not listed; call first.

records.name: Basic Needs Crisis Assistance and Client Choice Food Pantry
records.description_en: Helps Montgomery County residents in a money crisis with rent or mortgage, utilities, food from a client-choice pantry, prescriptions, clothing and transportation vouchers, and ID replacement.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For Montgomery County residents with an unexpected financial crisis. Rules vary by program.
records.how_to_apply: Call the appointment line or use the online appointment system on the CAC website.
records.notes: Business line (936) 539-1096; email info@cac-mctx.org. Serves all Montgomery County ZIP codes. Partner of Montgomery County Food Bank since 1985. Hours not listed on the official site; call first.

records.name: Emergency Shelter and 24-Hour Crisis Hotline
records.description_en: Free, confidential emergency shelter, a 24-hour hotline, counseling, and legal advocacy for survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault and their children.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For survivors of domestic or sexual violence of any gender in Fort Bend County and the greater Houston area.
records.how_to_apply: Call the 24-hour hotline at (281) 342-4357 for help or shelter.
records.notes: Office line (281) 344-5750; email help@fbwc.org. Office address on site: 501 East Hwy 90A, Richmond, TX 77406 (shelter location is confidential).

records.name: Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault Shelter and Hotline
records.description_en: 24-hour hotline, emergency shelter, counseling, advocacy, legal services, and transitional housing for survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For survivors of domestic violence or sexual assault in Montgomery County.
records.how_to_apply: Call the 24-hour hotline at (936) 441-7273.
records.notes: Also has an office at 1600 Lake Front Circle, Suite 130, The Woodlands, TX 77380. Transitional housing program: Reaching Pines. Cost not stated on the site.

records.name: Public Housing and Housing Choice Vouchers
records.description_en: Runs public housing and Housing Choice Vouchers (Section 8) that help low-income families pay rent in Galveston.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income households; waiting lists open only at certain times. The public housing list was listed as open for elderly applicants only.
records.how_to_apply: Apply online through the GHA portal when a waiting list is open. You can sign up to be notified when lists open.
records.notes: Site stated the Public Housing waiting list opened August 5, 2026 and remains open for elderly applicants only. Check the site for current waitlist status.

records.name: Conroe Connection Half-Fare Transit Card
records.description_en: Seniors, people with disabilities, Medicare card holders, and students can ride Conroe city buses for half price ($0.50 instead of $1.00). The first card is free.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For seniors 65+, Medicare card holders, people receiving SSDI or SSI, and students.
documents_needed: Completed Half-Fare application (short or long form)
Valid government photo ID
Medicare card (if using Medicare to qualify)
Social Security letter showing SSDI or SSI (if using disability to qualify)
records.how_to_apply: Bring the completed form, photo ID, and qualifying document to the City of Conroe Transportation Department. Show your card every time you board.
records.cost: First card free; replacement $5. Half fare $0.50 one-way
records.notes: Starting September 2, 2026, in-person transit services temporarily moved from 300 W. Davis to 202 Avenue A, Conroe. CityRides Commuter (Route 291) discounted fare is $4 one-way (no cash).

records.name: Conroe Connection ADA Paratransit
records.description_en: Shared rides for people with disabilities who cannot use the regular city bus, within 3/4 mile of Conroe bus routes. Fare is $2.00 one-way.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people whose disability keeps them from using the fixed-route bus. A health care professional must certify the application.
documents_needed: ADA paratransit application with health care professional certification
records.how_to_apply: Email the completed ADA application to Transit@cityofconroe.org. Once approved, book rides from 7 days ahead up to the day before.
records.cost: $2.00 one-way; personal care attendant rides free
records.notes: Both pickup and drop-off must be within 3/4 mile of Conroe fixed routes. Office temporarily at 202 Avenue A starting Sept 2, 2026 (regular address 300 W. Davis).

records.name: Fort Bend Transit Demand Response Service
records.description_en: Curb-to-curb shared rides anywhere in Fort Bend County for work, shopping, medical appointments, or other trips. Open to the general public, seniors, and people with disabilities.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to the public for trips within Fort Bend County. Children under 13 must ride with an adult.
records.how_to_apply: Call to register and book a ride 1 to 10 business days ahead. Give your name, address, pickup place, phone, destination, and appointment time.
records.hours: Reservations Monday-Friday 8:00am-4:00pm; service Monday-Friday, last pickup 5:00pm; no service on county holidays
records.cost: Fare not stated on source; ask when booking
records.notes: Phone listed as 281-633-RIDE (281-633-7433) or toll-free 866-751-TRIP (866-751-8747). Fares were not shown on the page; ask when booking. Six no-shows or late cancels in 90 days leads to a 30-day suspension.

records.name: Connect Transit Micro-Transit
records.description_en: On-demand shared rides in parts of Brazoria and Galveston counties, booked by app or phone. Seniors, students, and people with disabilities pay $0.50 in-zone.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to the public in GCTD service zones (including Lake Jackson, Freeport, Clute, Texas City, La Marque, Dickinson, Bacliff, San Leon). Reduced fare for seniors, students, and people with disabilities.
records.how_to_apply: Download the free 'Gulf Coast Transit District' app or call the scheduling team to book a trip. Trips outside your zone need 48 hours' notice.
records.cost: $1.00 in-zone; $0.50 seniors/students/disabled; children 6 and under free; outside zone $2.00 first 10 miles + $0.25/mile
records.notes: Also runs a Veterans service to Michael E. DeBakey VA Hospital ($3.50 one-way, weekdays 6am-6pm) and Park & Ride from Texas City ($2.00) and League City ($4.00). Email customerservice@gulfcoasttransitdistrict.com.

records.name: Brazos Transit District Demand & Response (Montgomery County)
records.description_en: Shared curb-to-curb rides for anyone in rural parts of Montgomery County outside the urban area, plus a free Town Center Trolley in The Woodlands.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to the general public and people with disabilities whose trip is in Montgomery County outside the urbanized area and not near a fixed route.
records.how_to_apply: Book online at btd.org or call customer service. Seniors and people with disabilities can ask about the Senior & Disabled Pass application.
records.cost: General public $3.50 one-way within county; $4.00 crossing 1 county; Town Center Trolley free
records.notes: Customer service extension 7008. Language assistance/accessibility: (800) 272-0039. Town Center Trolley info: (281) 210-3800. Reduced senior/disabled rates not listed online; call. Fare details from https://www.btd.org/demand-and-response/rates/.

records.name: Crisis Services and Psychiatric Emergency Treatment Center
records.description_en: The local mental health authority for Montgomery County. Offers a 24/7 crisis line and a walk-in crisis center open 24 hours a day in Conroe.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For people in Montgomery, Liberty, and Walker counties having a mental health crisis.
records.how_to_apply: Call the 24/7 crisis line or walk in to the Psychiatric Emergency Treatment Center.
records.hours: 24 hours a day, 365 days a year
records.cost: Sliding scale for people without insurance; co-pays as low as $0
records.notes: FM 2854 is also known as Old Montgomery Road/Metcalf Street. Call or text 988 for the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline.

records.name: Mental Health, Crisis, and IDD Services
records.description_en: The local mental health authority for Fort Bend County. Offers a 24/7 crisis hotline, adult and youth mental health care, autism and developmental disability services, and Early Childhood Intervention.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For residents of Fort Bend, Austin, Colorado, Matagorda, Waller, and Wharton counties.
records.how_to_apply: Call the main number to get services, or the 24/7 crisis hotline in an emergency.
records.notes: 24/7 Mental Health Crisis Hotline: (800) 633-5686. Call or text 988 for the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline.

records.name: Mental Health Services
records.description_en: The local mental health authority for Galveston and Brazoria counties. Offers a 24-hour crisis hotline and same-day or next-day mental health visits for adults and youth.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For residents of Galveston and Brazoria counties. Youth services are for ages 3-17.
records.how_to_apply: Walk in Monday-Friday for same-day/next-day intake (adults 8-10:15am and 12:30-2:45pm) or call the appointment line.
records.hours: Walk-in intake Monday-Friday: adults 8:00-10:15am and 12:30-2:45pm; youth 8:00-9:45am and 12:30-2:15pm
records.notes: 24-Hour Crisis Hotline: (866) 729-3848. Other adult clinics: 4700 Broadway #100, Galveston 77550; 101 Brennen Ln, Alvin 77511; 101 Tigner Rd, Angleton 77515. Youth clinics: 3201 FM 2004, Texas City 77591; 101 Tigner Rd, Angleton.

records.name: Lone Star Family Health Center
records.description_en: A federally qualified health center with family medicine, OB-GYN, dental, behavioral health, pharmacy, lab, and X-ray. Offers a sliding fee discount.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Open to everyone in the greater Conroe area; fees can be lowered based on income through the sliding fee program.
records.how_to_apply: Call to make an appointment at one of the sites in Conroe, Grangerland, Magnolia, Spring, Willis, or Huntsville.
records.notes: Six service sites; street addresses were not on the homepage.

records.name: Public Health Clinic
records.description_en: Provides childhood and adult shots, TB testing and treatment, HIV testing, and STD testing and treatment.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For Montgomery County residents.
records.how_to_apply: Call or visit the clinic during business hours.
records.notes: The site refers residents needing health care help to the county Indigent Care / Health Care Assistance Program (HCAP).

records.name: Free Civil Legal Aid
records.description_en: Free lawyers for low-income people with civil problems such as evictions, housing, and public benefits.
records.eligibility_summary_en: For low-income people who meet financial and legal status rules. Civil cases only (not criminal).
records.how_to_apply: Apply online or call the toll-free intake line.
records.notes: The Conroe, Galveston, and Richmond offices have closed; residents apply online or by phone. The Clute office serves Brazoria County. Local Houston line: (713) 652-0077.

records.name: Workforce Solutions Conroe Career Office
records.description_en: Free help finding a job, job training scholarships, and child care financial aid for working parents and people in school or training.
records.eligibility_summary_en: Job search help is open to anyone. Child care aid and training have their own income and work/school rules.
records.how_to_apply: Visit the office or call. You can also call the main line 1-888-469-JOBS (5627).
records.notes: Main line 1-888-469-5627. Workforce Solutions serves the whole 13-county Gulf Coast region; any office can help.
